title: ‘I see a different Bart Verbruggen’: Brighton’s Hurzeler impressed by No 1’s transformation
content:
Fabian Hurzeler says Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen has improved “in every phase of his game” this season.

Verbruggen was at fault in allowing a shot from Bukayo Saka to deflect past him via team-mate Carlos Baleba in Arsenal’s 1-0 win at the Amex Stadium in Brighton’s last fixture.

It was a rare blemish for the 23-year-old Netherlands No.1 during a campaign in which Hurzeler has noticed Verbruggen’s progress under goalkeeper coach Jelle ten Rouwelaar, the pair having previously worked together at Anderlecht. Verbruggen has played in all 29 league games, keeping six clean sheets.

“In every phase of his game, in possession he makes much more calm decisions, more right decisions than he did before. Out of possession, he’s much more present,” Hurzeler, the Brighton head coach, told The Athletic during his press briefing for Saturday’s match at Sunderland.

“He’s made some great saves during the season so far.

“Of course, there have been one or two mistakes but regarding his development I see a different personality in the goal, I see a different Bart Verbruggen who gets a better understanding of the game, a better understanding of making the right decisions and who is just an incredible goalkeeper when it comes to making saves.

“Therefore, I am very happy with his development, with his performances so far. He is a very ambitious guy, he wants to improve, he tries to reflect on everything, to be 100 per cent professional in every part of his life. I see a bright future for him.”

Leading European clubs, including Bayern Munich, have been linked with Verbruggen, but Hurzeler is not fearful of losing his goalkeeper if he performs well for the Netherlands at this summer’s World Cup.

“I am not worried, because that’s part of this game, it is also part of this club,” Hurzeler added. “If young players develop faster than we do as a club, then there will always be bigger clubs who go for this player. In the end it’s also a positive thing if big clubs try to get our players, because it shows a lot of good things regarding recruitment and the good work my coaches do with him.”

Verbruggen will not be facing Dutch international rival Robin Roefs against Sunderland.

Roefs, also 23, is ruled out for the third match in succession by injury. Brighton are 14th in the table, three places below Sunderland, but they would move above their hosts on goal difference with a second successive away victory at the Stadium of Light.
